The drawings establish an independently supported passive water product and an independently supported slow feeder, each with its own base and removable underside pad. F-I is a separate removable insert, and C is a detachable connector rather than shared structural support needed for either product to stand. Drinking and eating surfaces remain open from above. Silhouettes and obstacle paths may vary; merged products, a shared indispensable base, or an integral nonremovable insert fail.

Visible geometry and annotations establish matching vertical side patches on the left and right of both bases, centred along side depth, with 36 mm width and 20 mm height, spanning z = 6–26 mm. Each horizontal open recess measures 28 x 4 x 3 mm and is centred at z = 16 mm. C engages facing recesses across a 2 mm connection-plane gap in the dry exterior zone. Opposite patches permit reversal with the same parts; bowls lift upward without dismantling their bases. Clip exterior design may vary, but inaccessible or tool-dependent release, missing opposite patches, or altered fixed geometry fails.

A readable map assigns a specific proposed material grade, finish and intended water/food-contact or dry-exterior zone to W-B, W-R, W-P, F-B, F-R, F-I, F-P and C. The bowls share a proposed material family, base finishes share a family, and two distinct removable non-slip elastomer pads attach beneath their respective bases in dry zones. Material and manufacturing choices are open proposals; missing assignments, generic material labels without grades, or incompatible paired assignments fail.

Every image board includes NESTPAIR in its title. Assembly and clip-detail boards also carry the exact handling warning; on assembly-cleaning it sits beside the clip-removal step. Typography and title layout may vary. A name appearing only on a depicted physical product does not satisfy the title requirement, and an absent or misplaced required warning fails.

Front, top and right orthographic views correspond to one complete design, with separate W, F and C views. Readable dimensions establish the individual and joined maximum envelopes, a clear circular W-R well of diameter 150 mm and depth 35 mm, a circular F-R well of diameter 140 mm and depth 25 mm, F-I rise no greater than 18 mm, every food path at least 12 mm wide, and the 2 mm connection gap. W-R visibly locates its 350 mL fill mark below the rim. Bodies may be smaller than the maximum envelopes; conflicting views, omitted dimensions, or geometry outside the specified bounds fail.

Both sheets map the same eight IDs to the same service parts. Numbering or arrows clearly order emptying both vessels, detaching C and separating products, lifting both bowls upward, removing F-I, removing both pads, hand washing, rinsing, separately air drying all eight parts with bowl interiors exposed, and dry reassembly. Reassembly restores pads to their correct bases, F-I to F-R and bowls to their own bases before final reconnection. Integrated grips and release features are allowed; extra service parts, swapped IDs, inaccessible washing surfaces or an out-of-order sequence fail.

D1 places the joined, bowl-seated W-left/F-right pair fully within a 400 x 220 mm mat. DR1 fits exactly the eight separated service parts within a 500 x 400 mm draining surface, with F-I detached and both empty bowl interiors exposed. ST1 fits dry, complete, unconnected products side by side in a 400 x 240 x 160 mm cabinet opening, each on its own base and pad, with C beside them and independently accessible. Area annotations or clear dimensional evidence establish fit; exceeding boundaries, missing parts or blocking clip retrieval fails. Scene context remains a neutral compact home; an animal is optional.

W and F maintain a calm domestic family through related rims, grips, seams and exterior finishes across drawings, diagrams and scenes. The same eight-part design remains recognizable through assembled use, separated drying and reassembled storage, with no replacement components. The two bowls share a material family, the bases share an exterior finish family, and each removable elastomer pad belongs beneath its own base.
